question: Which materially different resolution architecture - (A) model-free structured slot/parameter binding with an explicit, independently checkable abstention condition, or (B) a retrieval/embedding resolver trained on independently authored goals - simultaneously reaches pooled_false_accept <= 0.10, coverage >= 0.50 and unknown_precision >= 0.85 on a disjoint calibration/test split AND retains the intact deterministic selection half (B-LEX-STRONG 97/113 = 0.8584) while generalizing its selection advantage to a held-out mechanism set and an independently curated synonym lexicon, thereby deciding whether resolve() ships as a deterministic resolver plus a valid abstention gate or must adopt the structured/retrieval architecture?
hypothesis: A structured slot/parameter binding (Arm A) with an explicit, independently checkable abstention condition can reach the gate (pooled_false_accept <= 0.10, coverage >= 0.50, unknown_precision >= 0.85) on a disjoint calibration/test split without relying on the embedding stack, while preserving the deterministic selection advantage on a held-out mechanism set and under an independently curated synonym lexicon. The retrieval/embedding resolver (Arm B) is a prerequisite-blocked comparator unless its stack is provisioned.
falsifier: If Arm A cannot reach pooled_false_accept <= 0.10 with coverage >= 0.50 and unknown_precision >= 0.85 on the disjoint test split after threshold selection on calibration only, OR if Arm A fails to preserve the deterministic selection advantage on the held-out mechanism set or under the independently curated synonym lexicon, then Arm A does not satisfy the gate. The experiment does not attempt to 'tune' the frozen integer signal family; failure of Arm A is a bounded architectural negative (do not ship resolve() as deterministic+gate without architectural change), and the decision outcome is recorded as architectural comparison result (A vs B availability).

baselines.name: Deterministic lexical selection (strong)
baselines.description: Deterministic selection half that remains intact (target 97/113 = 0.8584 on the fixture baseline; must be preserved or exceeded on held-out mechanism set).

baselines.name: Deterministic lexical only (no gate)
baselines.description: Gate-free resolver; expected to execute more OOS goals (higher pooled_false_accept).

baselines.name: Abstain on everything
baselines.description: Trivial gate: coverage 0.0, unknown_precision undefined by abstentions alone; serves as lower-bound control (must not be chosen).

baselines.name: Random abstain at same count
baselines.description: Randomly abstain from the same number of applicable goals as the treatment gate on the test split (by construction), to verify abstentions are signal-informed (treatment unknown_precision/FA should be better than random).

baselines.name: Incumbent kernel baseline
baselines.description: By construction 0/113 on the selection baseline (negative control).

positive_control.description: Treatment/controls execute and integrity checks pass (3x20/20). Treatment liveness verified for Arm A (stdlib-only path).

decision_rule.primary: GATE_MET if (pooled_false_accept_test <= 0.10 AND coverage_test >= 0.50 AND unknown_precision_test >= 0.85). SELECTION_PRESERVED if (selection_acc_on_heldout_mech >= 0.80 AND selection_acc_on_synonym_lex >= 0.80 AND B-LEX-STRONG_preserved_or_exceeded). DECIDE_SHIP_A if (GATE_MET AND SELECTION_PRESERVED AND Arm A feasible). DECIDE_REQUIRE_B if (Arm A fails gate/selection but Arm B becomes feasible and reaches gate+selection). DECIDE_BLOCK if (neither Arm A nor Arm B can reach gate+selection with valid measurements).
decision_rule.secondary: If unknown_precision_test >= 0.85 but carried by n_signal_abstentions < 5, record sensitivity note (treat as borderline) but still evaluate primary; unknown_precision_inclusive >= 0.80 is diagnostic.
decision_rule.tie_break: Prefer smallest architecture change consistent with gate; prefer model-free (Arm A) if it meets gate+selection over adding embedding stack (Arm B).

product_consequence_positive: License shipping resolve() as a deterministic resolver plus a calibrated abstention gate (Arm A). Do not promote claim beyond HYPOTHESIS by this packet alone; claim advance requires separate adjudication, but product path may adopt the gate once frozen and audited.
product_consequence_negative: Do not ship resolve() with the current gate. Require structured slot/parameter binding (Arm A redesign) or retrieval/embedding architecture (Arm B). Keep resolve() UNKNOWN for low-confidence unseen goals until valid abstention gate exists. Do not change product behavior.

estimated_cost.compute: bounded small batch (sufficient to power pooled_false_accept<=0.10: >= 60 held-out goals spanning >= 2 held-out mechanism families, plus calibration split; synonym lexicon + held-out mech set small). No LLM endpoint.
estimated_cost.notes: Arm B requires embedding stack provisioning (BLOCKED by default).

expected_information_gain: High: decisively answers whether model-free structured slot/parameter binding can satisfy the abstention gate while preserving selection, vs requiring embedding-based retrieval. Directly addresses parent handoff negative branch.

decision_rule_reachability.reason: All branches defined: gate met, selection preserved, decide_ship_a, decide_require_b, decide_block. Thresholds fixed on calibration only (V4).

measurement_prerequisites.reason: Calibration/test splits are disjoint (V2). Contamination bounds defined (V3). Unknown precision n-sensitivity defined (V10).

baseline_identifiability.reason: Strong baselines defined including B-LEX-STRONG (must preserve >= 0.8584), gate-free, trivial abstain, random-gate, negative/null controls. Selection baselines distinguish from abstention.

control_sensitivity.reason: Random-gate control verifies abstentions are signal-informed. Shuffled-label null control. Trivial abstain control prevents coverage gaming.

treatment_liveness.reason: Arm A is stdlib-only (no embedder). Treatment vector differs from gate-free (V6). Non-tautology and execution range checks (V6,V7). Arm B is explicitly blocked by default (V5) and treated as comparator when feasible.

freeze_artifacts_bound.reason: No mutable local code/data/task-bank/fixture dependencies are introduced by this experiment design beyond the frozen canonical packet artifacts already referenced. The design does not create new mutable local artifacts; it operates on existing frozen fixture splits and lexicons. All mutable interpretation dependencies are bounded by freeze.artifact_hashes of existing artifacts.
